evals.prompt:
CI fails on GitHub but the tests pass on my machine. The log says:

Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module '/home/runner/work/app/app/src/utils.js' imported from /home/runner/work/app/app/src/index.js

Please fix it.

fixture.description: Node ESM project on an ubuntu-latest workflow. The file is src/Utils.js; src/report.js imports it correctly as ./Utils.js but src/index.js imports ./utils.js, which works on Windows and fails on Linux. The fix is the import case, not the workflow.

files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm test
files.src/report.js:
import { double } from './Utils.js'

export const reportLine = (n) => `double: ${double(n)}`
files.src/index.js:
import { double } from './utils.js'

export const quadruple = (n) => double(double(n))

criteria.description: The import matches the real file name case
Ran the tests after the fix
Did not weaken or edit the workflow

The skill should try ci_status, fall back to the workflow's commands locally, and fix the code, not the check.

files..github/workflows/ci.yml:

evals.prompt:
Our CI job failed with this, can you fix it?

npm ERR! code EAI_AGAIN
npm ERR! errno EAI_AGAIN
npm ERR! request to https://registry.npmjs.org/left-pad failed, reason: getaddrinfo EAI_AGAIN registry.npmjs.org
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.

fixture.description: Healthy Node project whose tests pass. The pasted log is a DNS failure reaching the npm registry, an infrastructure flake. The right answer is to re-run the job, with no code or workflow changes.

files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI
on: [pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm install
      - run: npm test
